faq: Where do the reviews come from?
From your own store, review app or marketplace listing, exported by you. We use genuine customer reviews only, and we never write or buy reviews.
Will the summary hide bad reviews?
No. It reports the mix honestly, including common complaints. Hiding or editing negative feedback would mislead shoppers and break the rules of most platforms.
Judge.me, Yotpo, Loox, Stamped, Shopify Product Reviews and WooCommerce reviews are common examples. If yours can export a CSV, we can work with it.
How many reviews does a product need?
A summary becomes useful from around ten reviews. For products with fewer, we leave them out rather than overstate what a handful of comments say.

desc:
Customer review summaries for products condense the reviews you already have into a short, honest overview of what buyers like and dislike. Ecom Swift LLC reads your genuine reviews, writes a clear summary for each product and can show it on your product pages.

## What is a customer review summary?

A customer review summary is a short text that sets out what many reviewers say about a product: the common praise, the repeated complaints and any remarks about fit or size. It sits above the full list of reviews and points back to them.

It is a reading aid, not a replacement. A shopper who sees three lines can decide quickly, and a shopper who wants detail can still open every review.

## Why long review lists fail busy shoppers

Reviews are among the most useful content on a product page, but they are hard to use at volume. A product with two hundred reviews hides its main message inside paragraphs that nobody reads in full. Shoppers skim a few, usually the newest or the most extreme, and form a skewed picture.

Owners face the same problem from the other side. The same complaint, such as a zipper that sticks or a color that looks different on screen, may appear dozens of times, yet nobody has counted it. A summary brings repeated points to the surface for the shopper and for you.

## What a trustworthy summary includes

- A short list of what customers like, in the words they use.
- A list of common complaints, written without softening.
- Fit and sizing remarks, such as whether an item runs small.
- Links back to the original reviews, so shoppers can check the source.
- A note on how many reviews were read and when the summary was last updated.
- Review sources kept separate, so reviews from different channels are not mixed without a label.
- No edits that hide problems or invent praise.
- Plain language that matches the tone of the product page.
- Collection level highlights that show patterns across a range.
- A private note for you on issues that keep returning.

## How we work

We start with an export of your reviews from your review app or store. We read them product by product, group the points that appear again and again, and ignore one-off remarks that do not represent the wider view. Reviews that look false or off topic are set aside and listed for you, and we do not rewrite what real customers wrote.

Each summary is checked against the reviews it came from, and we keep the evidence so you can see the source of every claim.

The Basic package delivers plain summaries for your most reviewed products as a sheet. The Standard package covers more products, shows the summaries on your product pages with links to the original reviews, adds a private note on repeated issues and updates the text once with new reviews. The Premium package covers store-wide summaries that refresh on a schedule, adds collection level highlights and writes a report on the top problems worth fixing in the products themselves.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep negative points in the summary, because shoppers notice when they are missing.
- Use the private issues note to improve products, packaging or sizing guides.
- Refresh summaries as new reviews arrive.
- Link every summary to the full reviews.
- Collect reviews from real, verified buyers.

**Avoid:**
- Removing or hiding unfavorable reviews.
- Summarizing products that have only a handful of reviews.
- Adding praise that no customer wrote.
- Mixing reviews from unrelated products.
- Using the summary as a way to answer complaints you have not fixed.

## Who this is for

It suits a store with popular products and a long review list that shoppers rarely read. It suits an owner who suspects a recurring defect but has no time to read hundreds of comments. It also suits a brand that wants to show real feedback in a compact form on its product pages.

## What we need from you

Send a review export or tell us which review app you use. Share any rules about what may appear on product pages. We never ask for passwords. Exports are enough to start, and if you want the summaries shown on your pages, you add us as a collaborator, staff or developer user with limited permissions. A short checklist follows your order.
